items.titleEn: Gold, silver extend losses as tech stocks slide, Fed inflation test looms - Kitco PM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold and silver prices were sharply lower in late U.S. trading Tuesday, reversing Monday's recovery as stronger-than-expected U.S. consumer confidence, renewed concerns about trade tariffs and another technology-led equity selloff pressured precious metals. Gold fell below $3,600.00 an ounce, approaching last week's 14-month low, while silver suffered heavier losses as weakness in industrial commodities and broader portfolio liquidation compounded the selling. Bullion failed to benefit from a softer U.S. dollar and slightly lower Treasury yields as investors reduced exposure to metals ahead of Wednesday's important U.S. inflation data. At approximately 4:50 p.m. EST, spot gold was trading near $3,552.50 an ounce, down $81.70, or 2.25%, while silver was trading near $40.790, down $2.250, or 5.22%, on the session. Gold traded as low as $3,546.00 during the day, while silver touched $40.570. Tuesday's U.S. economic data indicated a substantial improvement in consumer confidence and modestly stronger regional manufacturing activity, reinforcing expectations that underlying economic demand remains resilient despite elevated borrowing costs. The Conference Board's November consumer confidence index surged 11.4 points to 103.3 from an upwardly revised 91.9 in October , substantially exceeding expectations near 92.5 and reaching its highest level since January 2025. The present situation index increased to 132.8, while the expectations index rose to 83.6, reflecting improved assessments of business conditions and the labor market. The Richmond Fed's manufacturing index also strengthened to 3 from minus 2 in October, with new orders improving to 2 from minus 8 and employment rising to 6 from 3. Meanwhile, September house prices were unchanged on the month, while the national Case-Shiller index increased 2.1% from a year earlier, below the prevailing inflation rate. The combination of improving consumer sentiment, modest manufacturing expansion and subdued housing-price growth highlighted the uneven economic outlook, although the stronger confidence figures reduced immediate concerns about a sharp slowdown in consumer demand.

items.titleEn: Gold's selloff is sowing the seeds of its next rally – Theo's Iggy Ioppe
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - The gold market continues to struggle to attract consistent bullish momentum as expectations that the Federal Reserve will maintain its hawkish monetary policies into the new year have driven real yields and the U.S. dollar higher, increasing the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset. However, Iggy Ioppe, Chief Investment Officer of Theo Network, a financial and tokenization platform, said that while gold has room to move lower in the near term, investors shouldn’t ignore the long-term, real-world value of holding the precious metal. He added that while most investors are familiar with the old commodity market cliché that “the cure for high commodity prices is high prices,” the opposite is also true, especially when it comes to gold.

items.titleEn: Huang tells staff that Nvidia does not need a succession plan
items.summaryEn: Buy a basket short NVDA exposure via relative value: short NVDA vs a peer basket like AMD (AMD) + Broadcom (AVGO) (long) and/or use an AI/semiconductor ETF long like SOXX while keeping NVDA as the underperformer. The news is company-specific governance/key-man risk; peers won’t face the same “founder too big to fire” narrative, so NVDA should lag on any governance-driven de-rating. Key Risk: A broader AI/semiconductor selloff overwhelms relative effects and drags peers down with NVDA. Sell NVDA. Huang publicly dismisses succession planning as “flawed,” despite filings warning that lack of succession planning can hurt execution. The stock already priced a “founder premium” rebound; now the market will demand a visible, investor-grade succession/oversight plan. Until the board names a credible internal successor/deputy or formalizes leadership depth, the key-person discount returns and multiple compresses.

items.titleEn: Michael Burry maintains Nvidia short thesis despite Jensen Huang's return
items.summaryEn: Buy Tencent (TCEHY / 0700.HK). Burry calls it a “Fortress business” and still undervalued despite AI spending. The second-order angle: if AI spend pressures near-term margins, the market discounts too hard; Tencent’s cash generation and platform moat should absorb the spend and stabilize earnings, making the valuation gap mean-revert. Key Risk: AI spending fails to translate into monetizable products and user growth, causing sustained margin compression and a prolonged earnings reset. Sell NVDA and/or stay short using bearish puts. Even with Jensen Huang back, the core thesis is governance risk plus accounting/antitrust overhang; the rally is leadership optics, not fundamentals. Burry’s own move—cutting puts after the spike but keeping the thesis alive—signals the downside case is still intact while uncertainty remains.

items.titleEn: HSBC, J.P. Morgan and StoneX complete first live trades using Pooled Gold Interests (PGI)
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – Gold ’s digital evolution passed a major milestone on Tuesday after HSBC, J.P. Morgan and StoneX conducted wholesale-market transactions using Pooled Gold Interests (PGI) for the first time. PGI is the underpinning of the World Gold Council’s Wholesale Digital Gold initiative, and Tuesday’s pilot transactions represent a significant step towards a new way for institutions to own, transfer and use gold. “Loco London physical 400-ounce Good Delivery gold bars were placed into the Wholesale Digital Gold ecosystem, and PGI were created, giving participants proprietary interests over pooled gold,” the WGC said in its announcement. “Once the transactions were settled, the gold was withdrawn from the ecosystem, completing the full lifecycle.”

items.titleEn: Dollar Tree stock jumps 12% as strong store traffic lifts profit outlook
items.summaryEn: Buy Dollar Tree (DLTR). The stock jumped on a real demand signal: store traffic +3.8% vs +0.4% last quarter, and comps +4.6% with ticket size only +0.8%—so growth is coming from more visits, not just higher spend. Management raised FY2026 adjusted EPS to $8.05–$8.25 (from $7.70–$8.05) and lifted revenue guidance. Multi-price expansion ($1.25/$3/$5+) is aligning with value-seeking behavior ahead of the holidays. Key Risk: Fuel and freight costs spike enough to erase the margin gains from higher traffic, forcing another guidance cut. Buy Dollar General (DG) vs DLTR. If DLTR’s traffic recovery is the start of a broader “discount demand” cycle, DG should benefit too, but DLTR already ran to a 52-week high—DG has more room to catch up if the theme keeps working into the holiday season.

items.titleEn: BCA Research ends four-year bullish gold trade as US dollar, Fed take their toll
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - One of the market’s longest-standing gold bulls is officially moving to the sidelines after last week’s selloff pushed prices to a fresh 14-month low, testing support at $3,500 an ounce. In a research note published Friday, Roukaya Ibrahim, Chief Commodities Strategist at BCA Research, said that she is now neutral on gold after being stopped out of her long position when prices dropped below $3,700 an ounce. BCA has been cautious on gold through most of the year as prices have fallen sharply from their record highs around $5,600 an ounce. The Montreal-based research firm saw some initial bullish potential in August, but gold’s momentum quickly faded.
